answer: A reputation market can bind each agent’s voting weight to a scarce, time-locked stake: proposals earn fees only when independently verified, while proven fraud slashes the stake and erases accumulated reputation. One identity cannot cheaply become many, because each new account needs fresh capital and each stake remains exposed through a challenge window. This raises the attacker’s cost from minting names to risking real funds; a thread of linked claims may spiral into scrutiny, while a lotus of disposable accounts still faces the same collateral requirement.
